Clepso design system · v0.2
Theme
Design system · v0.2 · September 29, 2026

A practice you can run from the courthouse hallway.

Clepso is the design system for the staff app (iOS and Android), the web app that follows, and the client app after that. It replaces the current dark navy-and-amber screens with a light-first, list-first system in cobalt and graphite, built around the four things the feature strategy says decide a small firm’s revenue: capturing time, getting paid, answering leads and keeping clients informed. Use the theme switch above to see every component and screen in light and in courthouse mode.

01 · Audit

Why the current system doesn’t hold up

The current app has one dark palette (navy canvas, amber accent, cream text), a four-step type scale on the system font, and nine primitives. Every screen is a stack of rounded cards on a dark background. It was a reasonable Phase-0 scaffold; it cannot carry a billing product that lawyers read in daylight, in court, and later on a 27-inch monitor. The findings below are ordered by how much they hurt.

1

No typographic system

The system font with four sizes (28 / 20 / 15 / 12) and no label, overline, amount or identifier styles. Numbers aren’t tabular, so amounts and hours wobble in lists; the timer uses a generic font-mono. Hierarchy comes from size alone, which is why every screen reads flat.

2

Card soup instead of lists

Matters, invoices, contacts and home sections are all floating rounded-lg bg-surface cards with 12px gaps and an 18px radius. A matter row costs ~90px, separators aren’t inset, and nothing distinguishes a list from a card from a tile. This is the “layout” problem: there is only one container, used for everything.

3

Dark-only, with hard-coded colours

The tokens file says “these ARE the dark theme values”; there is no light theme and the status bar is pinned light. Five hex literals (#FFB162, #1B2632, #8B94A3, #C9C1B1, #C96A50) are pasted into Button, Input, EmptyState, the tab layout and four screens, bypassing tokens entirely. Dense billing data on a phone in daylight needs a light theme; dark is the courthouse case, not the default.

4

The accent means everything, so it means nothing

Amber is the primary button, the warning colour, event icons, badges, unbilled amounts, filter chips, the active tab and the emphasis tile. Priority and overdue both use rust. Success is a muted olive that barely clears the surface. State and action share one hue, so nothing stands out. ink-faint on canvas is ~3.6:1, below the text minimum.

5

Two sources of truth, both incomplete

tokens.ts and tailwind-preset.cjs duplicate values with a “keep in sync” comment. Neither holds spacing, type, motion, elevation or sizes; neither has a light/dark structure; nothing is consumable by the web app without re-declaring it.

6

Navigation doesn’t match the strategy

Five equal tabs (Home, Matters, Tasks, Time, Billing). Capture is a whole tab with a timer and chips, not a one-tap action. Contacts hide behind the avatar; there is no calendar, no inbox, no lead surface. “Capture, don’t enter” needs capture reachable from every screen.

7

Nine primitives, no product components

Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, EmptyState, Input, Screen, SectionHeader, StatCard. No list row, segmented control, sheet, banner, toast, stage tracker, table, timer bar or form group. Badge is uppercase with wide tracking (shouty at 12px); Button has no icon slot or web sizes; Input has no affixes or states.

8

Details that add up

A full-amber “emphasis” tile competes with the primary button; section headers use the screen-title size; the tab bar is a fixed 84px with no safe-area logic; no focus states; no reduced-motion handling; demo credentials are printed on the sign-in screen.

What to keep
  • The 20pt screen gutter and the integer-minutes / integer-cents discipline in @lawfirm/core.
  • Dark mode as a real need. It becomes the second theme (“courthouse mode”), not the only one.
  • The stack: NativeWind, FlashList, the bottom-sheet library and the feature-slice structure all fit the new system without churn.
  • The idea of a running timer as a first-class object. It just needs to live on every screen instead of inside one tab.
02 · Direction

Clean, modern, exact

The strategy wants two sentences in the reviews: “the app works in court” and “I got paid faster”. Clepso should feel like a precise instrument: light paper-like surfaces, a cool graphite neutral ramp, one clear cobalt accent, hairlines instead of shadows, tight radii, one typeface at three weights, and tabular numbers everywhere. No decoration carries meaning that a word or a number could carry better.

Principle 1

Built for the hallway

One-handed reach, 44pt targets, the primary action at the thumb, glanceable state through pills and dots, and a dark theme that doesn’t light up a courtroom. Nothing destructive is one tap.

Principle 2

Money and time are type

Amounts, hours and identifiers have their own styles: tabular figures, dimmed cents, mono numbers. Every amount has a status next to it. Every hour has a rate behind it.

Principle 3

Lists first, cards for the exception

Grouped lists with hairline separators carry the product. A card marks the one thing that isn’t a list item: the running timer, Review your day, a deadline, a trust warning.

Principle 4

Colour is a promise

Cobalt means “act” or “selected”. Green means paid or done. Amber means within a week. Red means late or at risk. Teal means court or system. Nothing else is coloured.

Principle 5

Plain language, disclosed AI

Client-facing copy names the next dated event. AI suggestions are grey, labelled, and applied only by hand. The disclosure line lives where the rule requires it.

Principle 6

One system, three surfaces

The same tokens drive mobile, web and the client app. Web adds density and multi-pane layout; the client app softens the voice. Nothing is redrawn per platform.

Colour Cobalt on graphite

One accent

Cobalt #2B52D9 in light, lifted to #88A3FF in dark so it passes on dark surfaces. It appears on one filled element per view, on selection, on links and on the current stage. Everything else is graphite.

Four reserved states

Success, warning, danger and a teal info hue. Teal was chosen so court dates and system notices never read as the blue accent. Status colours never decorate and never appear in charts.

Graphite neutrals

A cool ramp (hue ≈ 222°) that leans toward the cobalt without competing with it. Light canvas #F7F8FA, ink #1C2029; dark canvas #12151B, ink #EEF0F4.

Typography two families, three weights

Geist · everything you read

High x-height, distinct numerals with real tabular figures, nine weights, excellent at 13–15px on both platforms. One family from the 11px overline to the 32px greeting; titles tighten to −0.02em so large text stays crisp. Ships as @expo-google-fonts/geist.

Geist Mono · records

Matter numbers, invoice numbers, UTBMS codes, account suffixes and the timer. It says “this is a record” without a label, and it keeps the timer from jittering.

Why no display face

The first draft used a serif for one line per screen. It read as editorial rather than modern, so it is gone: the greeting is now title-1 on mobile and display on web, in Geist. If a brand voice is wanted later it belongs in marketing and onboarding, not in the working screens.

03 · Navigation

Four places and one action

Mobile navigation is rebuilt around the strategy’s sequencing. Today is the daily loop (review captured time, agenda, who to nudge). Matters is triage and detail. Capture is the centre button on every screen. Calendar holds the docket and court dates. Billing is unbilled → invoices → payments → trust. Inbox (leads, client messages, approvals) starts as a header icon and takes the Calendar slot in H2 when the agenda folds into Today. Tasks and Time stop being destinations: tasks live in Today and inside matters; time lives in Capture and Billing.

Web mirrors the same model with a sidebar grouped into Work and Money, a ⌘K command palette, and the running timer in the top bar.

Tokens, type, space, elevation, icons

Everything below is generated from one file, design/src/tokens.py, into tokens.json (for Claude Design and future tooling), tokens.css (for web and these previews) and a contrast report. The mobile token file and Tailwind preset will be generated from the same source, so the “keep in sync” comment disappears.

Rules
  • One family for everything you read. Geist at 400/500/600 from 11px to 32px; titles tighten to −0.02em so large text stays crisp. No display face: the hierarchy is size, weight and space.
  • Numbers are always tabular. Amounts, hours, dates in columns, timers, KPI tiles. Cents render in ink-secondary so the dollars carry.
  • Identifiers are mono. Matter and invoice numbers, UTBMS codes, account suffixes. It says “this is a record”, not prose.
  • Weight before colour. Hierarchy comes from size and 400/500/600 weight; colour is reserved for state and action.
  • Uppercase only at 11px overline, with +0.06em tracking. Pills and labels stay sentence case.
  • Line length 45–70 characters on web; mobile body wraps at the 20px gutter.

Shadows mark the three things that float above the page: popovers, the running-timer bar and sheets/dialogs. In dark mode a 1px line-hairline ring replaces most of the shadow so edges stay visible.

05 · Components

The library

Forty component cards across six groups. Each renders live from the same stylesheet the screens use, in the accent and theme you picked above. The domain group holds the pieces that don’t exist in any generic kit and carry the strategy: the running timer, the Capture sheet, Review your day, Who to nudge, trust balances and invoices.

One primary per view. Secondary is tonal (no heavy outline) so groups stay calm. Destructive is tonal by default; the solid form is only for the confirming step of a dialog. Labels are verbs that name the outcome, and money in a label always shows cents.

Capture is the only raised, round, accent-filled control in the app. It opens the Capture sheet: timer, voice memo, time, expense, task, note.
Segmented controlIn-page tabs on mobile · block and scrolling forms

Segmented controls switch views of the same object (a matter, the billing area). Filters that narrow a list use chips instead.

08 · Implementation

From this page to the codebase

Nothing in the app has been changed yet; the system lives in design/ in the repo. With Cobalt and the name settled, the work is mechanical and lands in this order.

Sync to Claude Design

Run /design-sync, create a project called Clepso, and use design/system as the local directory. Every components/*/preview.html carries the @dsCard marker, so the Design System pane builds its cards on upload. Then generate the remaining H1 screens (calendar, contacts, matter tabs, payments, trust ledger, onboarding) against this system.

Generate the mobile tokens

Extend design/src/build.py to emit packages/ui/src/tokens.ts and packages/ui/tailwind-preset.cjs from tokens.py: colour tokens as light/dark pairs, spacing, radius, sizes, and the type scale as NativeWind fontSize entries. Delete the hand-kept duplicates.

Fonts and theme plumbing

Add @expo-google-fonts/geist, @expo-google-fonts/geist-mono and expo-font; load them in the root layout behind the splash screen. Add a theme provider (system / light / dark / courthouse) that sets NativeWind’s colour scheme and the status bar. Replace every hard-coded hex with a token.

Rebuild the primitives

In apps/mobile/src/components/ui: Button (variants, sizes, icon slot, loading), Field/Input (affixes, states), Pill, Chip, Segmented, Switch/Check, List/Row, Avatar, Section, Card, KpiTile, Banner, Toast, Sheet, Dialog, StageTracker, TimerBar, TabBar, EmptyState, Skeleton. Icons via phosphor-react-native.

Re-cut the navigation

Tabs become Today · Matters · Capture · Calendar · Billing with a custom tab bar (centre Capture button, docked timer bar). Tasks and Time tabs are removed; their content moves into Today, Matter detail, Capture and Billing. Inbox starts as a header icon.

Rebuild the screens against mock hooks

Today, Matters, Matter detail, Capture, Log time, Billing, Invoice, Sign in, then the client-app shell in apps/portal when it is scaffolded. The existing mock hooks keep working; only the presentation changes.

Web

When apps/web is scaffolded, it consumes the same Tailwind preset plus tokens.css, and ports the components as React + Tailwind with identical class vocabularies. Sidebar, top bar, table and drawer are the only new pieces.

09 · Open items

Settled, and what is left

Accent (Cobalt) and the name (Clepso) are decided and applied throughout. Two smaller calls remain; my recommendation is first in each.

1 · Tab bar in H1

Today · Matters · Capture · Calendar · Billing (recommended for H1: “bill from the courthouse”) · or swap Calendar for Inbox now if lead response ships earlier than planned.

2 · Mark

The placeholder mark is a cobalt tile with a “C” arc, set next to a tight Geist wordmark. It is deliberately simple and can ship in the staff app; a considered logo should replace it before the client app or any marketing goes out.
